annotation.title_clean: Privacy First: Designing Responsible and Inclusive Social Robot Applications for in the Wild Studies
annotation.title_en: Privacy First: Designing Responsible and Inclusive Social Robot Applications for in the Wild Studies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tonkin, M.; Vitale, J.; Herse, S.; Raza, S.A.; Madhisetty, S.; Kang, L.; et al.
annotation.venue: IEEE conference (RO-MAN 2019 likely); UTS OPUS repository
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper presenting a privacy-first user registration and login system for a Pepper social robot deployed in a government-run startup centre. Users chose face recognition or a QR code; the QR option increased adoption. It argues for transparent, privacy-compliant, inclusive social robot applications.
key_provisions_or_claims: Social robots in public spaces are effectively surveillance devices, so privacy must be addressed before deployment.
A registration system gave users control by offering a choice of face recognition or QR code.
81% of participants registering on the robot chose face identification, significantly above chance.
The QR code option increased the number of users adopting the technology.
Applications should be transparent, comply with local privacy law and be inclusive.
